info.bio:
The Selecter fue una de las bandas que protagonizó el fenómeno Two Tone, junto a The Specials, Madness, The Beat, Bad Manners y The Bodysnatchers, principalmente.

Originaria de Coventry, ésta se formó en 1979, como resultado de la suma de diversos músicos que provenían de músicas diferentes: Pauline Black, vocalista anglo-nigeriana, auténtico estandarte del grupo, Neol Davies, guitarra inglés y único miembro blanco de la banda, Charles Bembridge

scenes.name: 2-Tone: The Specials y el ska de los Midlands
scenes.book: Postpunk. Romper todo y empezar de nuevo
scenes.author: Simon Reynolds
scenes.desc: El sello de Jerry Dammers llenó en 1979 el hueco de un punk bailable: The Specials, siete músicos blancos y negros de Coventry (Terry Hall y su mirada heredada de Rotten, el rude boy Neville Staple), cruzan el ska de Prince Buster con la energía punk y un realismo social en blanco y negro («Gangsters», «Too Much Too Young», «Concrete Jungle», «Nite Klub»). El damero blanco y negro simboliza la integración racial; The Beat (Handsworth: «Mirror in the Bathroom», «Stand Down Margaret»), The Selecter («On My Radio») y Madness suman cinco hits en cinco singles. El sueño de un «nuevo Motown» se convierte en «un monstruo»: More Specials se refugia en la música ligera y la caja de ritmos, y «Ghost Town» (1981), retrato de la desindustrialización, llega al número uno mientras arden las ciudades. Fun Boy Three, «Nelson Mandela» y el fin. Posmoderno antes del new pop: «Estamos trayendo de vuelta algo que nunca existió».

mentions.book: Postpunk. Romper todo y empezar de nuevo
mentions.author: Simon Reynolds
mentions.text: …la banda de 2-Tone con el éxito más considerable y prolongado haya sido también la única formada exclusivamente por músicos blancos, mientras que The Selecter, cuyos integrantes eran todos negros -a excepción del guitarrista principal, Neol Davies, que era blanco-, fue la primera banda importante del movimiento en desaparecer por completo. The Selecter había tenido un hit muy considerable, "On My Radio", una canción con un sonido imprevisible que se quejaba de que las emisoras pasaran…

mentions.text: …originales de 2-Tone ya estaban desapareciendo: The Beac había lanzado su anémico segundo álbum -cuyo título, Wha'ppen [¿Qué pasó?], es revelador- y The Selecter simplemente se evaporó de la faz de la Tierra. Los únicos que seguían prosperando y creciendo eran Madness, quienes de a poco se fueron despojando…

podcast.title: British Music Press Championing
podcast.body: The Selector was a key band in the post-punk Ska sound, receiving significant promotion and support from the British music press. "SCA was one of the big post-punk sounds thanks to bands like the Specials and the Selector and Madness."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Mixed-Race and Mixed-Gender Lineup
podcast.body: The Selecter was one of the original two-tone ska bands from Coventry, England. Similar to their contemporaries The Specials, they featured a mixed-race lineup, but further distinguished themselves by also being a mixed-gender band. "Like their mates, the specials, the selector had a mixed race lineup. But they went further by being mixed gender."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Pauline Black's Diverse Career
podcast.body: Beyond her more than 40 years in music, Pauline Black has also hosted a TV quiz show for children, acted on both stage and television, and contributed to radio programming for the BBC. "Pauline has been active in music for more than 40 years, but she also hosted a TV quiz show for kids, acted on both stage and television, and has even done some work on the radio for the BBC."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Pauline Black's Identity and Stage Name
podcast.body: Frontwoman Pauline Black was born to an Anglo-Jewish mother and a Nigerian father, and was raised as Pauline Vickers by a white middle-class couple. She adopted the stage name Pauline Black both to conceal her musical activities from her boss, who disapproved of such pursuits, and to acknowledge her African roots. "She was brought up as Pauline Vickers, but adopted the stage name Pauline Black for a couple of reasons. First of all, she didn't want her boss to know that she was playing in a band. He apparently frowned on things like that. And to acknowledge her African roots."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
